title: Scalar subscript paths without an argument list
motivation: After the subscript specials went straight to their default method, `x[[i, j]] <- 5` still forced three operands, built an argument list of four cons cells, and ran `do_subassign2_dflt`. Reads such as `x[i, j]` and list stores went the same way, and only a vector store with one index had an allocation-free path (`Fir_subassign_scalar`). GNU-R bytecode has allocation-free scalar paths for all of these. matrix_for, binarytrees, bounce_nonames and storage showed the cost.
solution: `runtime.c` adds `Fir_subscript_scalar`, which copies GNU-R bytecode's scalar paths (`bcStackIndex`, `getMatrixDim`, `DO_FAST_VECELT`, `DO_FAST_SETVECELT`) for `[`, `[[`, `[<-` and `[[<-` with 1 or 2 scalar indices on a vector or matrix that is not an object. A read makes a new scalar or takes the list element, and a store writes in place, with `R_FixupRHS` for a list. `Fir_call_setter_builtin` keeps a short inline path for the static `x[[i]] <- v` with 3 arguments, so the function stays small and needs no stack array; every other shape calls `Fir_subscript_scalar` out of line, and anything else still takes the default method. Also in this range: a `SchedulePure` fix that never defers a statement to a use in a checkpoint's assumptions, so a deferred `box` no longer goes in front of them and leaves an `ldf` assumption unchecked.

files.client/rsh/src/fir2c/runtime.c: Adds `Fir_subscript_scalar` and its inline helpers for scalar reads and stores, uses them in the default-method path and setter builtin, and removes `Fir_subassign_scalar`.
files.server/src/main/java/org/prlprg/fir/opt/: `deferral` rejects a target that is a checkpoint assumption, and `placeBefore` no longer walks back over the leading assumptions.
files.server/src/test/java/org/prlprg/fir/opt/: Adds two tests: a `box` is not deferred in front of a checkpoint's assumptions, and a `box` that an assumption uses stays before the checkpoint.
files.server/src/test/resources/org/prlprg/exa: New `gcTorture` example whose lazy version had an unchecked `ldf` assumption after a deferred `box`.
New `gcTorture` example with scalar subscripts at the edges of the new paths: out-of-range or non-scalar indices, attributes, shared targets, coercing stores.
